html:
Maasina Rule was a movement for self-government and fair pay that began on Malaita in 1944 and spread across the Solomon Islands. The name means brotherhood in the Areʻare language.

Many of its founders had worked for the Americans in the Labour Corps during the Guadalcanal campaign and had seen higher pay and better treatment. They set up their own chiefs, courts and farming villages, and refused the head tax.

The British arrested its leaders in 1947 and 1948, but agreed in 1952 to a Malaita council. The movement is remembered as the start of Solomon Islands nationalism. Malaitans later moved in large numbers to Honiara.
sum: Maasina Rule was a movement for self-government and fair pay that began on Malaita in 1944 and spread across the Solomon Islands. The name means brotherhood in the Areʻare language.
